nodes.description: Public string state variable 'name' holding the ERC20 token name (DELOREAN).
Public string state variable 'symbol' holding the ERC20 token symbol (DLN).
Public uint8 state variable 'decimals' set to 18.
Public uint256 state variable '_totalSupply' holding the total token supply minted in the constructor.
Mapping 'balances' from address to uint tracking token balances.
Nested mapping 'allowed' from owner to spender to uint tracking ERC20 allowances.
Constructor: sets name, symbol, decimals and mints the whole _totalSupply to msg.sender.
totalSupply(): returns _totalSupply minus balances[address(0)]. Note: derived from the stored supply and the workaround for the known TOTALSUPPLY vulnerability.
balanceOf(address): view function returning balances[tokenOwner].
allowance(address,address): view function returning allowed[tokenOwner][spender].
approve(address,uint): writes allowed[msg.sender][spender] = tokens and emits Approval.
transfer(address,uint): debits msg.sender balance, credits recipient balance using SafeMath helpers and emits Transfer.

transferFrom(address,address,uint): debits 'from', reduces allowed[from][msg.sender] and credits 'to' without verifying the contract state's allowance check for the caller in the usual pattern (no require(allowed >= tokens) before SafeMath sub).
SafeMath.safeAdd(uint,uint): computes a+b and requires c >= a to guard overflow.
SafeMath.safeSub(uint,uint): requires b <= a then computes a-b.
SafeMath.safeMul(uint,uint): computes a*b and requires a == 0 || c/a == b.
SafeMath.safeDiv(uint,uint): requires b > 0 then computes a/b.
msg.sender: attacker-controllable caller used to key balances and allowed mappings and as minting recipient.
Arithmetic debit balances[msg.sender] = safeSub(balances[msg.sender], tokens) inside transfer.
Arithmetic credit balances[to] = safeAdd(balances[to], tokens) inside transfer.
Arithmetic debit balances[from] = safeSub(balances[from], tokens) inside transferFrom.
Arithmetic allowance decrement allowed[from][msg.sender] = safeSub(allowed[from][msg.sender], tokens) inside transferFrom; the preceding require-allowance check is absent.
Arithmetic credit balances[to] = safeAdd(balances[to], tokens) inside transferFrom.
Unchecked subtraction _totalSupply - balances[address(0)] inside totalSupply() with no SafeMath and no explicit underflow guard.

edges.reason: msg.sender is the mint recipient in the constructor: balances[msg.sender] = _totalSupply.
Constructor writes the token name state variable.
Constructor writes the token symbol state variable.
Constructor writes the decimals state variable.
Constructor assigns the fixed value to _totalSupply.
Constructor credits balances[msg.sender] with the minted supply.
totalSupply() reads _totalSupply.
totalSupply() reads balances[address(0)].
totalSupply() performs the unchecked subtraction _totalSupply - balances[address(0)] with no SafeMath, enabling potential underflow.
tokenOwner parameter is used to index the balances mapping.
balanceOf returns balances[tokenOwner] through the local return variable.
balanceOf reads from the balances state mapping.
tokenOwner parameter indexes the first dimension of the allowed mapping.
spender parameter indexes the second dimension of the allowed mapping.
allowance reads allowed[tokenOwner][spender].
allowance stores the result in the return variable remaining.
msg.sender keys the owner slot in allowed[msg.sender][spender] inside approve.
spender parameter is written into the allowed mapping.
tokens parameter becomes the approved allowance value.
approve writes the allowed state mapping.
approve returns true via the success return variable.
msg.sender is the debited account in transfer.
to parameter is the credited recipient in transfer.
tokens parameter is the transferred amount in transfer.
transfer performs safeSub on balances[msg.sender]; the debit depends on attacker-supplied amount.
transfer performs safeAdd on balances[to], an arithmetic credit path.
transfer writes the balances state mapping.
transfer returns true via the success return variable.
transferFrom keys allowed[from][msg.sender] with the untrusted caller but never requires the allowance to cover tokens before decrementing, allowing unsigned/derived-allowance abuse.
from parameter is the debited account and allowed mapping key in transferFrom.
to parameter is the credited recipient in transferFrom.
tokens parameter is the transferred amount in transferFrom.
transferFrom debits balances[from] via safeSub.
transferFrom decrements allowed[from][msg.sender] via safeSub without a prior allowance require.
transferFrom credits balances[to] via safeAdd.
transferFrom writes the balances state mapping.
transferFrom writes the allowed state mapping.
transferFrom returns true via the success return variable.
safeAdd operand a flows into the addition.
safeAdd operand b flows into the addition.
safeAdd assigns the sum to return variable c after the c >= a require.
safeSub operand a flows into the subtraction.
safeSub operand b is checked against a and used in the subtraction.
safeSub assigns a-b to return variable c after the b <= a require.
safeMul operand a flows into the multiplication.
safeMul operand b flows into the multiplication and overflow check.
safeMul assigns a*b to return variable c after the overflow require.
safeDiv operand a flows into the division.
safeDiv operand b flows into the b > 0 require and division.
safeDiv assigns a/b to return variable c.
transfer calls safeSub to compute the debit.
transfer calls safeAdd to compute the credit.
transferFrom calls safeSub twice; the second call on the allowance can revert when the allowance is insufficient, but no explicit require guards the allowance first.
transferFrom calls safeAdd to compute the credit.
